usageNotes: Use this to permanently destroy a QEMU VM and all of its owned disk volumes; the VM must be stopped first (use stop_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_status) or the API will return an error unless skiplock is set. The call is asynchronous — it returns a task UPID string that you should poll with get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status to confirm completion before treating the VM as gone. Pass purge=true to also remove the VMID from backup schedules, replication jobs, and HA configuration; omit it and those references will linger.

examples.summary: Destroy stopped VM 108 on pve1, purging all backup/HA references and scrubbing unreferenced disks

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes the VM configuration and all attached/owned disk volumes from storage; this action is irreversible and data cannot be recovered without an external backup.
tips: Always stop the VM before calling this endpoint; a running VM will cause the request to fail with a locked-VM error.
skiplock is root-only and should only be used to recover from a stuck lock after confirming the VM is truly stopped.
destroy-unreferenced-disks is false by default; enable it after cloning operations that may have left orphaned disk images with the same VMID.
The returned UPID can be polled via get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status to wait for full cleanup before reclaiming the VMID.
